children.text: Chapter 1
tṛtīye garbhamāse sīmantaṃ kārayate ||
children.translated_text: In the third month of pregnancy he has the <s>sīmanta</s> (hair-parting rite) performed.

children.text: śuddhapakṣasya puṇyāhe parvaṇi vā yathoktam upasamādhāya jayaprabhṛtibhir hutvā paścād agner darbheṣu prāṅāsīnāyāḥ sarvān keśān sampramucya prasādhayate yaṃ sīmantam iti
children.translated_text: On an auspicious day in the bright fortnight, or on a lunar observance day, he establishes the fire as prescribed and offers oblations beginning with the <s>Jaya</s> offerings. Then, behind the fire, he loosens all the hair of the woman seated facing east on <s>darbha</s> grass and arranges it, reciting, “The hair-parting which...”

children.text: yaṃ sīmantaṃ kaṅkatas te cakāra yad vā kṣuraḥ parivavarja vapaṃs te
children.translated_text: “The hair-parting that the comb made for you, or that the razor passed around while shaving you—

children.text: strīṣu rūpam aśvinau taṃ nidhattaṃ pauṃsyenemaṃ saṃsṛjataṃ vīryeṇa
children.translated_text: O <s>Aśvins</s>, place in her the beauty found among women; unite this woman with manly generative power and vigor.

children.text: indrāṇī cakre kaṅkataṃ sa sīmantaṃ visarpatu
children.translated_text: <s>Indrāṇī</s> fashioned the comb; may it extend the parting of the hair.

children.text: punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṃ dā agne prajayā saha
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, give the wife back to her husband together with offspring.

children.text: punaḥ patnīm agnir adād āyuṣā saha varcasā
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> has given the wife back, together with long life and splendor.

children.text: dīrghāyur asyā yaḥ patir jīvāti śaradaḥ śatam iti ||
children.translated_text: Long-lived is her husband; may he live for a hundred autumns.”

children.text: triḥśyetayā śalalyā śamīśākhayā sapalāśayā vā sīmantaṃ vicinoti yās te rāka iti ||
children.translated_text: Three times he parts her hair with a white porcupine quill or with a leafy branch of the <s>śamī</s>, reciting the verse beginning, “That which is yours, O <s>Rākā</s>...”

children.text: athāsyāḥ pṛthak keśapakṣau saṃnahyati nīlalohitena sūtreṇa nīlalohitaṃ bhavati kṛtyāsaktir vyajyate
children.translated_text: Then he separately ties her two side-locks with a blue-and-red thread, reciting, “It becomes blue and red; the attachment of sorcery is made manifest.

children.text: edhante asyā jñātayaḥ patir bandheṣu badhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Her relatives prosper; let her husband be bound in bonds.”

children.text: yo gurus tam arhayet ||
children.translated_text: He should honor the person who is the teacher.

children.text: etad eva kumārīṇāṃ saṭoddharaṇam atraivānulepanam ||
children.translated_text: This same rite is the raising of the braid for maidens; the anointing is also performed at this point.

children.text: Chapter 2
atha puṃsavanam ||
children.translated_text: Next comes the <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for engendering a male child).

children.text: bhūyiṣṭhagateṣu garbhamāseṣu trīn sthālīpākāñ śrapayed āgneyam aindraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: When the greater part of the months of pregnancy has elapsed, he should cook three <s>sthālīpāka</s> offerings: one for <s>Agni</s>, one for <s>Indra</s>, and one for <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ yathādevataṃ juhoti
children.translated_text: From these he offers an oblation to each respective deity.

children.text: agnis tuviśravastamam indra kṣatraṃ pra tad viṣṇuḥ
children.translated_text: He recites the formulas beginning, “<s>Agni</s>, most abundantly famed...,” “O <s>Indra</s>, dominion...,” and “<s>Viṣṇu</s> has extended that...”

children.text: pumān ity abhijuhoti
children.translated_text: He offers an additional oblation with the words, “A male.”

children.text: pumān agniḥ pumān indraḥ pumān viṣṇur ajāyata pumāṃsaṃ janayet putraṃ daśame māsi sūtave
children.translated_text: “Male is <s>Agni</s>; male is <s>Indra</s>; male was <s>Viṣṇu</s> born. May she bear a male son, to be delivered in the tenth month.

children.text: yena jātena vibhunā jīvema śaradaḥ śataṃ paśyema śaradaḥ śatam iti taṃ no maṃhasva śatinaṃ sahasriṇaṃ gosanim aśvasaniṃ vīraṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: With that mighty child born, may we live for a hundred autumns and see for a hundred autumns. Bestow him upon us, endowed with hundreds and thousands, a winner of cattle, a winner of horses, a hero. <s>Svāhā</s>.”
